name: Australian Open
summary: The Australian Open is the first of tennis's four Grand Slam tournaments each season, played on hard courts at Melbourne Park every January. It is run by Tennis Australia and was first held in 1905.

nameChange.text: Australasian Championships from 1905, Australian Championships from 1927 and the Australian Open from 1969

organiserFact.citation: Fast facts: Tennis Australia conducts tournaments including the Australian Open
organiserFact.editorNote: Also listed as the Australian Open's organising body in Appendix A of the 2026 Official Grand Slam Rule Book.

founded.editorNote: Became the Australian Championships in 1927 and the Australian Open in 1969 (same page). Not held 1916–18 and 1940–45.

format.text: Knockout singles draws of up to 128 players and doubles draws of up to 64; men's singles matches are best of five sets, other matches best of three
format.citation: Tournament Regulations, Article I C (Size of draws) and L (Number of sets)

venue.citation: Fast facts: moved to Flinders Park (now Melbourne Park) in 1988

name: Roland-Garros
summary: Roland-Garros, also called the French Open, is the Grand Slam tournament played on red clay at Stade Roland-Garros in Paris from late May into June. It is run by the Fédération française de tennis.

organiserFact.citation: Présentation générale: the FFT organises major tournaments including Roland-Garros

founded.citation: Palmarès: the men's singles roll of champions starts in 1891
founded.editorNote: Best known as the French championships, open only to members of French clubs until 1925; that detail is not confirmed on a page read.

format.text: Knockout singles draws of up to 128 players and doubles draws of up to 64; men's singles matches are best of five sets, other matches best of three
format.citation: Tournament Regulations, Article I C (Size of draws) and L (Number of sets)

frequency.text: Annually, from late May into early June
frequency.editorNote: The 2027 dates include the qualifying event.

name: Wimbledon
summary: Wimbledon, officially The Championships, is the Grand Slam tournament played on grass at the All England Club in south-west London over a fortnight each summer. First held in 1877, it is the oldest of the four.

organiserFact.text: The All England Lawn Tennis Club, under joint management with the Lawn Tennis Association
organiserFact.citation: The Championships: Management and Finances (Committee of Management)
organiserFact.editorNote: The Championships are under the joint management of the AELTC (through The All England Lawn Tennis Club (Championships) Limited) and the LTA (through LTA Operations Limited). The All England Club is not a governing body, so no organiser reference is set; the LTA (gb-lta) is a joint manager.

founded.citation: History: 1870s (the first Lawn Tennis Championship, at Worple Road)

format.text: Knockout singles draws of 128 players for gentlemen and ladies; men's singles matches are best of five sets, other matches best of three
format.citation: Tournament Regulations, Article I C and L
format.editorNote: 128-player gentlemen's and ladies' singles draws confirmed on the 2026 Wimbledon draw sheets (source-wimbledon-draws).

frequency.text: Annually, over a fortnight in the summer
frequency.citation: The origins of the All England Lawn Tennis & Croquet Club, p. 15 (13 days each year); 'the Fortnight'
frequency.editorNote: Usually late June to mid-July; exact dates not confirmed on a page read.

venue.text: The All England Club, Church Road, Wimbledon, London
venue.citation: History: 1920s (move from Worple Road to Church Road in 1922)

name: US Open
summary: The US Open is the Grand Slam tournament played on hard courts at the USTA Billie Jean King National Tennis Center in New York. It traces back to the first US national championship in 1881.

organiserFact.citation: Appendix A: tournament contacts list the USTA for the US Open
organiserFact.editorNote: An explicit 'owns and runs' statement was not found on usta.com or usopen.org on 2026-10-25; Appendix A gives the USTA's address with usopen.org as the US Open's contact.

founded.text: 1881, as the U.S. National Singles Championship for men
founded.citation: USTA History timeline: 1881; the U.S. Championships became the US Open in 1968

format.text: Knockout singles draws of up to 128 players and doubles draws of up to 64; men's singles matches are best of five sets, other matches best of three
format.citation: Tournament Regulations, Article I C (Size of draws) and L (Number of sets)

frequency.editorNote: Annual, late August to early September; usopen.org loads its dates by script and they could not be read on 2026-10-25
frequency.text: Annually, late August to early September

venue.text: USTA Billie Jean King National Tennis Center, Flushing Meadows, New York (since 1978)
venue.citation: About: home to the US Open
venue.editorNote: The move to Flushing Meadows in 1978 is in the USTA History timeline (source-usta-history).

name: ATP Tour
summary: The ATP Tour is the main circuit of men's professional tennis, a season of graded tournaments from ATP 250 to Masters 1000 that ends with the ATP Finals. It is run by the ATP.

organiserFact.citation: Rule 1.01: ATP Tour tournaments and ATP Challenger Tour tournaments are governed by ATP

founded.editorNote: Commonly given as 1990, when the ATP took over the running of the men's tour; atptour.com is behind a Cloudflare bot check and was not read on 2026-10-25. The Nitto ATP Finals history page confirms the 'ATP Tour World Championships' name from 1990 but not the tour's start.

format.text: A season of ATP Tour 250, 500 and Masters 1000 tournaments, plus the United Cup and the ATP Finals
format.editorNote: 2024 edition; the Grand Slams and Davis Cup are listed as separate categories of men's professional events.

name: WTA Tour
summary: The WTA Tour is the main circuit of women's professional tennis, a season of WTA 250, 500 and 1000 tournaments that ends with the WTA Finals. It is run by WTA Tour, Inc.

organiserFact.editorNote: WTA Tour, Inc. is a US corporation whose members are the players, its WTA 1000, 500 and 250 tournaments and the ITF.

founded.editorNote: The WTA itself was founded in 1973 (source-wta-website); when the tour took its present form under the WTA was not confirmed on a page read. The WTA history page loads by script.

format.text: A season of WTA 250, 500 and 1000 tournaments linked by a ranking points system, ending with the WTA Finals

frequency.citation: Structured data on the About page: WTA Tour 2026 season, 1 January to 31 December 2026

name: Nitto ATP Finals
summary: The ATP Finals is the men's season-ending event, where the eight best-placed singles players and doubles teams of the year meet in round-robin groups before knockout semi-finals and a final. It has been held in Turin since 2021.

nameChange.text: The Masters from 1970, ATP Tour World Championships from 1990, Tennis Masters Cup from 2000, ATP World Tour Finals from 2009, Nitto ATP Finals from 2017

organiserFact.citation: Terms and conditions: the site and the ATP Finals marks belong to ATP Tour, Inc.
organiserFact.editorNote: The history page (source-atp-finals-history) also names a former ATP Executive Chairman as the event's tournament director.

founded.citation: History: first Masters in Tokyo in December 1970

format.text: Eight singles players and eight doubles teams, in round-robin groups, then knockout semi-finals and final

frequency.text: Annually, at the end of the season in November

venue.text: Inalpi Arena, Turin (Turin is host from 2021 to 2027)
venue.citation: Site header; event overview gives the 2021–2027 run in Turin

name: WTA Finals
summary: The WTA Finals is the women's season-ending event, where the eight best-placed singles players and doubles teams of the year play round-robin groups of four before knockout semi-finals and a final. The host city changes; the 2026 edition is at Indian Wells.

organiserFact.citation: Section VI: The Tour Year culminates with the WTA Finals

founded.citation: Past winners: the singles list begins with the 1972 event (7–15 October)

format.text: Eight singles players and eight doubles teams in two round-robin groups of four; the top two of each group play knockout semi-finals and a final
format.citation: Section VI B 1: Singles and doubles competition formats

frequency.text: Annually, at the end of the season
frequency.editorNote: Recent editions have been held in late October and November; 2026 is 8–15 November (source-wta-finals-tournament).

venue.text: Indian Wells Tennis Garden, California (2026); the host city changes
venue.citation: Tournament page: WTA Finals is contested on the courts of the Indian Wells Tennis Garden; 8–15 November 2026

name: Davis Cup
summary: The Davis Cup is the international team competition of men's tennis, contested by nations through tiers with promotion and relegation and decided at an eight-nation Final 8 each November. It is run by World Tennis (formerly the ITF) and was first played in 1900.

organiserFact.text: World Tennis (formerly the International Tennis Federation)
organiserFact.citation: About World Tennis: the Davis Cup is run by World Tennis

founded.citation: USTA History timeline: 1900, first International Lawn Tennis Challenge (Davis Cup) match, United States v British Isles at Longwood Cricket Club
founded.editorNote: daviscup.com/en/about says '1990', an evident typo; not used.

format.text: Nations play in tiers (Final 8, Qualifiers, World Groups I and II, regional groups) with promotion and relegation; home-or-away ties are best of five matches, and eight nations contest the Final 8 in one host city

frequency.text: Annually; the Final 8 is held in November
frequency.citation: About: format (Qualifiers in February and September, Final 8 in November)

venue.text: Final 8 in 2026: BolognaFiere, Bologna; ties below it are played home or away
venue.citation: Davis Cup Final 8: all you need to know

name: Billie Jean King Cup
summary: The Billie Jean King Cup is the international team competition of women's tennis, run by World Tennis (formerly the ITF). Launched in 1963 as the Federation Cup, it ends each year with an eight-nation knockout Finals.

nameChange.text: Federation Cup 1963–1995, Fed Cup 1995–2020, then the Billie Jean King Cup

organiserFact.text: World Tennis (formerly the International Tennis Federation)
organiserFact.citation: About World Tennis: the Billie Jean King Cup is run by World Tennis

founded.citation: About: launched in 1963 for the ITF's 50th anniversary

format.text: Qualifiers of home-or-away ties (best of five matches) lead to an eight-nation knockout Finals; other nations play Play-offs and regional groups

frequency.citation: About World Tennis: one of the two largest annual international team competitions in sport

venue.text: Finals in 2026: Shenzhen, China; Qualifiers are played home or away

name: United Cup
summary: The United Cup is a mixed team event that opens the season in Australia each January, with 18 nations each fielding men and women in singles and mixed doubles. Group matches are split between Perth and Sydney, which stages the final.

organiserFact.editorNote: Commonly described as run by the ATP, the WTA and Tennis Australia. The site is owned by ATP Tour, Inc. and the 2024 ATP Rulebook lists the United Cup among ATP Tour tournaments (source-atp-rulebook-2024), but no page read names the organisers.

founded.editorNote: The first edition ran from late December 2022 into January 2023; the 2027 event is billed as the fifth edition (source-united-cup-overview).

format.text: 18 national teams in round-robin groups of three in two cities, then knockout rounds; each tie is a men's singles, a women's singles and a mixed doubles

frequency.text: Annually, at the start of January

venue.text: RAC Arena, Perth, and Ken Rosewall Arena, Sydney

name: Olympic tennis
summary: Tennis is played at the Summer Olympic Games in five events: men's and women's singles and doubles, and mixed doubles. It was on the programme from 1896 to 1924 and returned as a full medal sport in 1988.

organiserFact.editorNote: Part of the International Olympic Committee's Summer Games, with World Tennis (ITF) responsible for the tennis event; Olympedia says the ITF assigned quota places and wild cards in 2021 (source-olympedia-tennis-2020), but no IOC or ITF page naming the organiser was read (olympics.com did not respond on 2026-10-25).
organiserFact.text: International Olympic Committee, with World Tennis (ITF)

founded.citation: Overview: tennis at every Games from 1896 to 1924, back as a full medal sport in 1988
founded.editorNote: World Tennis also says tennis returned as a full medal sport in 1988 (source-daviscup-world-tennis).

format.text: Five knockout events: men's and women's singles (64 players), doubles (32 pairs) and mixed doubles (16 pairs); singles best of three sets

venue.text: Changes with each Games; Stade Roland-Garros, Paris, in 2024
